assertions.name: selfnormalized_is_a_measure
assertions.source: Sum_lambda dim_q^2/Sum_mu dim_q^2 = 1 for every n in the atom set — true by construction, checked numerically

assertions.name: textbook_equals_c_n_times_selfnormalized
assertions.source: w_textbook(lambda) = c_n * w_selfnorm(lambda) exactly, every lambda, every n — the identity the cross-atom distortion follows from

assertions.name: scaling_law_reproduces_recorded_textbook_run
assertions.source: self-normalized per-atom ratios scaled by c_n reproduce the INDEPENDENTLY RECORDED textbook-normalized cross-atom max/min (1.8217); tolerance 1e-3 because the recorded ratios carry only 4 significant figures

description: The balanced-convention q-Plancherel normalization gap (bean qou-7o7h). dim_q^2/[n]_q! is NOT a probability measure in the balanced q-integer convention: c_n = Sum dim_q^2/[n]_q! runs 0.991 / 1.111 / 1.517 at n = 6/9/12 and GROWS with n. Because w_textbook = c_n * w_selfnormalized exactly and the binding functional is linear in the weights, B scales by c_n; the factor cancels within one atom but NOT across atoms, since n = 3A differs. So any cross-atom metric — the max/min variance the FR-pullback probes are scored on — is distorted. Measured: the published 1.82x baseline is ~53% inflated by this alone; the self-normalized figure is 1.19x, and the scaling law reproduces the textbook run to 5.5e-5 (that residual being the 4-sig-fig rounding of the recorded ratios). Says nothing about which normalization is physically right — only that the two differ by a known n-dependent factor and the corpus contains both.

ratio_identity_shortcut.status: TRUE BUT CONDITIONAL — do not quote as the mechanism
ratio_identity_shortcut.condition: holds only while the argmax atom is the largest-c_n atom and the argmin atom the smallest, under BOTH normalizations
ratio_identity_shortcut.quote_instead: w_textbook = c_n * w_selfnormalized, and the functional is linear in the weights

caveats: The reconstruction's inputs (per-atom self-normalized ratios, recorded textbook max/min) are READ FROM a prior run of fr_pullback_borromean_h3a_test, not recomputed here — that would need the ~25-minute H_12 character leg. The scaling law itself (assertion 2) is computed from scratch and is what carries the finding; the reconstruction is a consistency check on top of it.

Those recorded ratios come from a run at the RETIRED muon-era pin A, while c_n here is computed at the current proton pin. The 11.5 ppb pin difference is ~7 orders below the effect being measured (a 53% inflation), so it cannot affect the conclusion — but the reconstruction is therefore a cross-pin comparison and its 5.5e-5 residual should not be read as a precision claim.
